corpus_estimate.note: post-stratified by language (weights = live translated pages per language at draw time); languages outside the 15 sampled are not represented; CI = 95% bootstrap over pages-as-books within language

sensitivity.note: corrected estimates; see comment in score.mjs. "language" = the headline weighting; "language_x_arm" re-weights the quota-sampled arm to its true share; "page_weighted" weights each book by its translated pages (random page rather than random book)

worst.reason: translation renders a different passage (the next page of the speech); none of the source's content (learned institutes, 'Karl der Geliebte', star of the first magnitude) appears
Translation is of a different passage (head lice and Chapter V catarrh remedies); the source's ulcer remedies are entirely absent.
verses 10–15 rendered faithfully apart from 'jitāsuḥ' as 'conquered his senses'; the commentary above and below the verses, roughly half the page, is dropped entirely; Sanskrit read moderately
repeat marks rendered literally as 'each and every one' make the first entry and many quotations nonsense; Feng Yi quotation garbled; later entries (五十難, 迫難) roughly right

Each quoted line is roughly rendered, but from 雲咽 onward the headwords shift one entry against their citations, and four headwords are lost, so a reader learns the wrong compound for nearly every quotation.
translates only the Bhagavata verses 25–33, loosely, and drops the whole commentary; v.33 'did not comprehend' inverted to 'attained this knowledge'; v.30 Hara clause and v.28 list dropped
First column rendered accurately, but the whole second column (about half the page) is absent

builds a fluent narrative (Choi clan woman, funeral, procession, 'Hyeon-ha' title) on a garbled transcription the source cannot support; only the Yeong dismissal and Nang-wang's arrogance track the source
§9's opening is faithful, but the footnote is dropped and replaced by invented continuation text.
Opening sentence and footnotes are dropped, and the second triad is completed from text that is not on this page.
only the mūla verses 35–38 and ch.3 vv.1–2 are translated; roughly half the page (Śrīdhara commentary) is missing
pp. 188-189 rendered accurately, but about as much again of text from later pages is added after 'How wise'; that is imported content.

What is translated (Clermont theses on infallibility, §24 on the Catechismus Gratiae 1650) is accurate, but the papal condemnation of Jansen's Augustinus and the 1661 Jesuit context that open the page are missing entirely.
The 熊虎狀, 毅狀 and 風雲狀 quotations are right, but the main headword 萬狀 is misunderstood across seven quotations and headings are invented.

The poets and titles are correct, but the lexicon's headword, which is the subject of the entry, is replaced throughout by an invented 'shanshan / field and mountain', so every quotation says something the source does not.

The source transcription is largely garble; the translation turns it into fluent but unsupported narrative (Dodang meeting wives, house of righteousness). My reading of the handwritten Korean is moderate.

Nutmeg and pepper are roughly right, but the rhaponticum/rhubarb chapter is misidentified with invented degrees, the pepper degrees and 'third class' are invented, and several clauses are misread. Abbreviated incunable Latin, so moderate confidence.
The source is largely garble (repeated 츳). The translation turns it into fluent dialogue and adds a named speaker and a plot. Little of this is supportable. I read cursive Hangul weakly.
This is a loose summary of the opening commentary that drops verse 7's substance and all of the later commentary; I read the Sanskrit only moderately well
the source is a near-meaningless OCR string; the translation builds a coherent narrative of sacrifice, prosperity and wine that the source cannot support; my reading of this archaic hangul is weak
The source is a garbled transcription of Korean cursive, and the translation turns it into fluent but unsupported sentences plus an invented summary. I read this handwritten script weakly.
Only the 淵浩 and 淵曠 entries (Song shu, Qi shu, Wei shu Xu Zunming, Shen Yue) are rendered properly; a non-existent 'Yuan Chong' headword is invented and three entries are dropped.
Systematically renders ☋ (cauda draconis) as the zodiac sign in all four entries; also 'interfectionem' becomes 'intersection'. The ☊ and comet clauses are otherwise faithful.
English-to-English; imports a clause from the previous page and drops a sentence, otherwise verbatim.
Most compound entries are right (毗騫 kingdom, 騰騫, 低騫, 縶騫, 陳騫), but the whole 無騫 entry is misread as 'increase/decrease'.
